considered.name: Refinancing Cliff Risk for Innovators
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, dlc)), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A research-intensive firm fails not when its cash is low but when maturing obligations arrive before its research pays off; the share of near-term liabilities not covered by cash measures a funding cliff that must be met by asset sales or dilution precisely because knowledge capital cannot be pledged, so cheap innovators without a cliff are undervalued and those with one are correctly discounted.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the persistent cash-level statistic the critic showed would be collinear with its own five-year minimum, and instead uses the maturity structure of debt — `dlc` relative to the cash available to retire it — which no archive signal has touched and which varies for reasons (refinancing calendars, credit-line draws) largely independent of the cash-to-assets level. The ratio is bounded in [0,1] with a well-behaved denominator, equals zero for firms with no current debt, and is gated by R&D intensity so the funding-cliff interpretation applies only to firms running an unpledgeable investment program.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Stock Vintage Value
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), COALESCE(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 2), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge capital depreciates quickly, so two firms with identical R&D stocks differ economically depending on vintage: one whose stock is concentrated in the last two years owns current-generation technology, while one whose stock is mostly five years old holds capital that capitalization schedules overstate and competitors have already imitated.
considered.reasoning: The critic is right that a floor on R&D intensity is just the persistent intensity level in disguise; vintage share is a *composition* statistic that is deliberately scale-free — it is invariant to how much a firm spends and varies only with the time profile of that spending, so it cannot proxy for intensity or for the R&D-versus-no-R&D split. Non-reporting firms have an undefined ratio and are assigned zero, which is the economically correct reading (no fresh knowledge) rather than a coverage patch.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Replacement-Cost Cheapness of Knowledge Capital
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che)), NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The economic capital a buyer would have to reproduce is tangible assets plus accumulated knowledge capital, excluding purchased intangibles that reflect past transaction prices rather than reproduction cost; when enterprise value sits far below that reproduction cost, the market is refusing to pay for capital that demonstrably exists.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the turnover-in-disguise construction with a genuine valuation anchor the archive lacks — a replacement-cost (inverse-Q) numerator rather than an earnings, sales, or realizable-asset numerator — and it avoids the fragile low-revenue denominator by dividing by enterprise value, which is bounded away from zero for essentially all firms. Pairing it with the already-validated peer-excess soft-book conditioner holds the conditioner fixed, so the evaluation isolates the new anchor's contribution.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Trough Pre-Research Earnings Cheapness
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_MIN(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A value signal should ask whether a firm is cheap against the earnings it produces in its worst year, not its most recent or its average year; for intangible-intensive firms whose reported earnings are depressed by expensed research and lumpy product cycles, trough pre-R&D earnings relative to price is the conservative measure of what the buyer is guaranteed.
considered.reasoning: The malformed averaging construction is replaced by a downside statistic, which is the transformation the archive has shown to work repeatedly on conditioners (margin floor α 5.4%, pre-research earnings floor α 5.4%) but which has never been applied to the value leg itself — and it is explicitly not the published cyclically-adjusted average earnings yield, since a trough and a mean rank firms very differently when earnings are skewed. Holding the conditioner identical to Signal 3 makes the two proposals a clean head-to-head on which new valuation anchor carries more information.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self-Built Minus Purchased Capital Value
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: The two ways a firm can acquire intangible capital have opposite valuation implications: self-built knowledge is expensed and therefore invisible in book value, while purchased intangibles are capitalized at negotiated prices that embed a control premium, so the signed difference between organic and acquired intangible intensity measures how much economic capital the accounting hides net of how much it overstates.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 rank-difference version of this idea produced the archive's then-largest alpha (6.4%) but a null FMB slope (0.31) on only 9% coverage, because it used a multiplicative product with an `oancf` value leg; expressing the composition as a single continuous raw difference inside an additive composite should restore both the cross-sectional slope and full coverage. The measure is defined for every firm — a purely tangible firm scores exactly zero — and is economically distinct from the peer-excess soft-book conditioner because it nets the hidden asset against the overstated one rather than measuring either alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Creditor-Adjusted Knowledge Asset Backing
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Equity holders own realizable assets only after creditors are paid, so the correct backing for a share price is net cash — cash less all debt — plus accumulated knowledge capital; a firm whose net liquid and knowledge assets approach its market capitalization is one where the market assigns no value to the operating business and no leverage claim stands ahead of the buyer.
considered.reasoning: The gross version of this anchor earned α 5.6% (t 5.02), but it credits cash to equity holders even when it is fully offset by debt, and the gen-5 failure of the replacement-cost anchor (α 1.1%) suggests exactly that leverage contamination is what destroys asset-based anchors. Subtracting total debt converts the numerator into a genuine residual claim rather than a gross asset count, which is an economic correction to the claim structure rather than a rescaling, and the margin floor is held fixed so the comparison against the gross anchor is clean.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Peer Innovator Interaction With Margin Floor
considered.expression: SUMRANK(MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che)), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The cheap-innovator-among-peers interaction identifies where knowledge capital is unpriced, but it cannot distinguish an unpriced innovator from one whose research supports a commoditizing product line; adding a downside pricing-power screen should convert its strong cross-sectional signal into a tradable spread.
considered.reasoning: The conjunctive peer-innovator product has the highest FMB t-stat in the archive (6.93) but only α 4.1%, a diagnostic signature of a signal whose ranking is right on average but whose extreme deciles contain deteriorating businesses — precisely the failure the margin floor screens out. This hybridizes the two structural families rather than stacking two conditioners: the multiplicative interaction supplies the peer-relative mispricing signal and the additive floor supplies the survival screen.

considered.name: Cheapness as a Binding Constraint
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), MIN(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, dlc)), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(TS_MIN(GROWTH(revt, 1), 5), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: In every archive composite, cheapness enters compensatorily, so a firm can reach the long leg on extreme cheapness alone — which for intangible-intensive firms is precisely the distress signature; if cheapness is instead treated as one more constraint that must be satisfied, the long leg becomes firms that are adequately cheap, adequately funded and adequately demanded, and the value premium should be cleaner.
considered.reasoning: The critic is right that swapping conditioner slots inside the existing MIN signal tests nothing new, so this changes what the conjunction is applied *to*: the value leg itself is now inside the minimum rather than carrying half the composite weight, which is a different economic claim (no attribute can be compensated) and produces a materially different long leg that excludes the deepest-discount names. It also directly addresses the recurring diagnostic in this archive that value-heavy composites deliver strong FMB slopes but tail-driven alphas.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Safety Hurdle Count
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), ADD(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, dlc))), -0.5), ADD(INDICATOR(TS_MIN(GROWTH(revt, 1), 5), 0), INDICATOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5), 0.2))))
considered.hypothesis: Survival of an intangible program is governed by discrete hurdles rather than by continuous rankings: cash must cover near-term debt, revenue must never have contracted, and the margin floor must remain above a level where pricing power is real; the number of hurdles cleared, not the average percentile across them, is what distinguishes a genuine undervalued innovator.
considered.reasoning: This fixes the weighting miscalibration the critic identified — the three INDICATOR terms carry exactly equal weight by construction, so the comparison against the minimum-rule signal is now a clean test of conjunctive degree versus binding constraint — and it replaces a generic rank blend with economically calibrated absolute thresholds rather than cross-sectional percentiles. The coarse 0-3 score also produces far more stable portfolio membership than continuous ranks, which matters given that several archive signals show strong slopes with unstable tails.

considered.name: Research That Shows Up In Margins
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Research creates knowledge capital only when it produces a product competitors cannot match, and the observable proof is that a firm both out-invests and out-prices its industry peers; a cheap firm satisfying both is one whose expensed research has demonstrably become an economic asset, while a cheap heavy spender with peer-average margins is funding a program that has not differentiated anything.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the IND_RANK knob-turn on the funding gate and instead tests an unexamined economic claim — that the informative interaction is between research effort and *realized differentiation*, both measured against direct competitors — which is distinct from the failed intangible-productivity conditioners because those scaled profit by a capital base (turnover) whereas margin isolates pricing power. Both legs are industry-ranked so the conditioner cannot become a bet on inherently high-margin or research-heavy sectors, and coverage remains full since non-reporting firms simply rank at the bottom of research effort.

considered.name: Unproductive Soft Book Penalty
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt))), 0))))
considered.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles are not inherently bad accounting: a soft book is only evidence of overpayment when the acquisitions failed to buy pricing power, so the penalty for intangible intensity should apply solely to firms whose gross margins sit below their industry peers, and successful acquirers should not be penalized at all.
considered.reasoning: Every soft-book conditioner in the archive applies an unconditional linear penalty, which necessarily mismarks the profitable roll-up that genuinely bought a franchise; making the penalty state-contingent on below-peer margins is a new economic claim about *when* accounting softness signals overpayment. The indicator switches the penalty on and off rather than blending two ranks, so the resulting ordering is materially different from both the peer-excess soft-book signal and the margin conditioners it borrows from.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Backing With Collateral Screen
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Realizable liquid and knowledge assets relative to price is a sound valuation anchor, but the buyer needs assurance that creditors will not consume those assets; that assurance belongs in a separate screen measuring debt against pledgeable tangible collateral, not inside the anchor's numerator where it swamps the asset content.
considered.reasoning: This is the diagnosed repair of the gen-6 failure: subtracting total debt from the numerator turned the anchor into a net-leverage factor with fmb 0.59 and Sharpe 0.03, whereas the gross anchor alone earned α 5.6% (t 5.02) with a 3.89 slope. Moving the creditor adjustment into a bounded conditioner preserves the anchor's cross-sectional information while still excluding the levered firms whose knowledge stock belongs economically to lenders.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Earnings Suppression Reinvestment Share
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: The degree to which accounting understates a firm's earning power is governed by how much of its gross profit pool it routes into expensed research: a firm reinvesting half its gross profit reports earnings roughly half of its economic earnings, so among firms already cheap on pre-research earnings, high reinvestment share marks those whose reported EPS most badly misleads screening investors.
considered.reasoning: All prior intangible-intensity conditioners scale research by assets, which measures capital-structure-like intensity rather than the size of the accounting distortion; scaling by the gross profit pool measures exactly the wedge between reported and economic earnings, which is the mechanism named in the research brief. It is well-defined at full coverage (gross profit is positive for nearly all firms), is zero for non-researchers, and is not a profitability ratio since it holds the profit pool in the denominator.

considered.name: Persistently Cheap Innovator
considered.expression: SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, dlc)), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))

critic_notes.rationale: This is a textbook rediscovery of intangible-adjusted book-to-market (Lev–Sougiannis, Peters–Taylor intangible capital, Eisfeldt–Kim–Papanikolaou "Intangible Value"), and as a single-theme value ratio it offers no cross-theme content beyond a known published anomaly.

The z-score difference collapses approximately to R&D-stock-to-market equity — itself a documented anomaly (Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis) — and the stated orthogonality to plain BM is false because the two z-scores are divided by different industry standard deviations, leaving residual BM-level exposure.

Value × intangible-intensity is essentially the same intangible-value mechanism as proposal 1 in conditional clothing, and because the ranks are not demeaned the product loads heavily on the two main effects (mostly BM) rather than isolating the interaction it claims to test.

Economically coherent as a value × asset-turnover composite (which is close to standard value-plus-quality practice), but `intan` is not COALESCEd so coverage will be silently truncated to intangible-reporting firms, and the denominator `intan + RD stock` approaches zero for tangible firms, making the ratio a winsorization artifact rather than a measure of intangible productivity.

The pairing of an R&D-added-back earnings yield with a goodwill-intensity conditioner is a defensible and reasonably distinct cross-theme mechanism, though the large mass of zero-goodwill firms creates a big rank tie block that reduces the conditioner to a near-constant for much of the cross-section, so the test is effectively earnings yield with a short leg of goodwill-heavy acquirers.

The dynamic pairing of a relatively conservatism-immune sales-to-price multiple with a multi-year intangible-productivity trend is the most genuinely novel construction here, but the unscaled TREND slope is mechanically proportional to the level of revenue-per-intangible, so the second leg should be normalized (e.g., slope divided by the series mean) or it will partly rediscover the level signal in proposal 4.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Yield x Organic-minus-Acquired Intangible Mix
critic_notes.rationale: The signed organic-minus-acquired composition score is a genuine structural fix to the gen-0 winner's degenerate zero-goodwill tie block rather than a cosmetic re-parameterization, and switching the value leg to pre-R&D operating cash flow is an economically motivated (not merely mechanical) attempt to convert a strong cross-sectional slope into a reliable portfolio alpha, though it remains close enough to the archived winner that a null result would be uninformative.

This is the archived "Demeaned Value x Off-Balance-Sheet Capital Share" with the R&D scaler swapped from an asset-stock to sales and, more seriously, with the expected sign reversed post hoc to match the previously observed negative estimate — that is sign-fitting to a known result rather than a new hypothesis, and BM interacted with R&D-to-sales is itself a long-published interaction (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis).

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Profit Yield vs Implied Intangible Price
critic_notes.rationale: The stated mechanism is internally inconsistent — because the two legs are separately rank-transformed, the "identical denominator" never cancels and cannot produce a price-versus-payoff spread, leaving what is operationally a conventional industry-neutral gross-profitability-minus-valuation composite (Novy-Marx plus value) whose second leg is also ill-behaved when market value falls below book equity.

The core hypothesis — high-valuation firms making goodwill-generating acquisitions subsequently underperform — is the published glamour-acquirer/asset-growth anomaly (Rau-Vermaelen; Cooper-Gulen-Schill), and the ZSCORE product additionally lumps cheap firms taking goodwill *impairments* into the same extreme tail as expensive serial acquirers, so the signal's short leg conflates two economically distinct populations.

critic_notes.target_name: Scale-Free Intangible Productivity Trend vs Sales Price
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnosis of the gen-0 failure is specific and correct (raw TREND scales with the series level, and the `intan` denominator both truncated coverage to 8% and created near-zero-denominator artifacts), and normalizing the slope by its own five-year mean plus re-basing on total assets plus the R&D stock is a real fix — but the mean-normalized trend can still blow up for firms with low average intangible productivity, and the sales-to-price value leg is unchanged, so the alpha problem may well persist.

This is a near-duplicate of the archived "Cheapness x Intangible-Inclusive Gross Profitability" — the same industry-relative intangible-inclusive gross profitability conditioner on a value leg, differing only by ZSCORE-versus-RANK and BM-versus-EBITDA/P — which is precisely the cosmetic variant of an already-failed signal (ls_talpha −0.55) that the objective warns against.

This is a one-input swap on the gen-1 "Cash Yield x Organic-minus-Acquired Mix" whose resulting expression is also nearly the archived "Organic R&D Earnings Yield" with an added +RANK(R&D-stock/at) term — a term the archive's "Demeaned Value x Off-Balance-Sheet Capital Share" result suggests loads negatively — so it is a cosmetic recombination of two evaluated signals rather than a new mechanism.

Combining two independently validated conditioners under an additive rank composite is incremental rather than conceptually new, but the linear-vs-product construction question is a real and testable diagnostic for the archive's recurring "strong FMB slope, weak alpha" pattern; note the nested SUMRANK implicitly weights the value leg 1/2 and each conditioner 1/4, which should be stated deliberately.

The conditioner NEG(Δgoodwill/at) is largely a repackaging of the well-published acquisitiveness/asset-growth anomaly, and the hypothesis is internally muddled because falling goodwill conflates value-creating divestitures with impairments, which the impairment literature shows are followed by continued underperformance — the opposite of the stated "bad news already realized" logic.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Capital Cheapness Backed by Profits
critic_notes.rationale: The value leg (R&D stock to market value) is a direct rediscovery of Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis / Lev-Sougiannis R&D-to-market, and mechanically the large mass of zero-R&D firms all receive the same tied low rank so that across most of the cross-section the product degenerates into a plain three-year ROA (profitability) sort.

Resolving whether the archive's adverse value x intangible-intensity interaction is a book-to-market artifact or a genuine obsolescence effect is a worthwhile first-order question and industry-ranking both legs is a substantive design change, but the two legs share xrd in the numerator, so part of any result will be mechanical co-movement rather than a true conditional effect.

NEG((xrd - ebitda)/at) is algebraically (ebitda - xrd)/at, i.e. essentially an operating-profitability conditioner, so despite the external-finance-dependence framing the signal reduces to the long-documented cheapness x profitability ("quality at a reasonable price") combination and overlaps heavily with the ROA conditioner proposed in the same batch.

This is the archive's gen-2 Hard-Book Value composite with one extra already-tested leg bolted on and the implicit weights shuffled from 1/2-1/4-1/4 to 1/4 each — a reweighting exercise that stacks previously-selected winners rather than testing a new mechanism, and the newly added margin-stability leg is also unwinsorized unlike its standalone version.

Swapping global RANK for IND_RANK on the existing best composite is precisely the kind of cosmetic single-knob variant the objective warns against; it may be a useful diagnostic but it proposes no new economic content and its outcome is largely predictable from the known sector concentration of goodwill and R&D.

The motivation (removing xrd from both legs to kill mechanical overlap) is legitimate, but the additive rank-sum contradicts the stated conjunctive hypothesis ("most research capital *while* trading at the lowest multiple") — a firm extreme on either leg alone scores high — so the construct reduces to an equal blend of two already-known effects (EV/EBITDA cheapness and R&D-to-assets intensity) rather than a peer-relative interaction.

This is the first genuinely new measurement dimension in the archive — time-series rather than cross-sectional cheapness — and the conditional multiplicative form matches the comparability-noise hypothesis, though the test should control for the fact that TS_RANK of E/P is mechanically a low-price-relative-to-own-history variable and thus partly a restatement of long-horizon reversal/negative momentum.

NEG(MA(GROWTH(csho))) is the net share issuance anomaly (Pontiff-Woodgate, Daniel-Titman), one of the best-documented published predictors and partially spanned by FF5's investment factor, so the composite is likely to be driven by a rediscovery rather than by the intangible-financing mechanism claimed.

The economic idea (program smoothness distinct from program size) is reasonable and distinguishable from the TS_COUNT persistence signal, but VOL(xrd/at) is unscaled by its own mean — unlike the margin-stability signal that motivated it — so the conditioner mechanically loads on R&D level and partially cancels the intensity rank it is multiplied by, muddying what the stability leg actually measures.

Economically coherent, but this is essentially the archived Cash-Insured Innovation Value (α 6.9%, t 5.26) with `che` swapped for `che − debt` inside the same multiplicative R&D gate and the same value leg — a one-variable substitution that is closer to a cosmetic variant than to the claimed "unification," and the two parents' distinct information (cash buffer vs. debt covered by *tangible* assets, not total assets) is lost rather than combined.

critic_notes.target_name: Reliable Book and Durable Moat Value
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical SUMRANK stack of two already-validated archive legs (Peer-Excess Soft Book Value and Value With a Margin Floor) with no new mechanism, and the nested SUMRANK also halves each conditioner's effective weight relative to its parent, so a null result would be uninformative about the orthogonality claim it is framed to test.

Value combined with (industry-adjusted) gross margin level is close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented gross-profitability/quality-plus-value pairing (Novy-Marx, QMJ), and it is also the most obvious simplification of two already-accepted margin conditioners, so it is both largely known and near-trivial.

The realizable-asset-to-price anchor (cash plus capitalized R&D stock over market cap) is a genuinely different valuation numerator from anything in the archive and the margin-floor gate is a coherent economic screen, though the reviewer should note the numerator's two components each map onto published anomalies (cash-to-price and R&D-to-market), so any result must be checked against those as controls.

Revenue-growth volatility is a quantity-side moat proxy that is economically distinct from the archive's margin-based conditioners, the expression is scale-free and its sign matches the hypothesis, and the only caveat is partial overlap with known fundamental-volatility/quality effects.

Because `xad` is missing for the large majority of firms and is coalesced to zero, the advertising leg's RANK degenerates into a reporting-availability/consumer-industry indicator rather than a measure of brand-capital intensity, so the multiplicative "dual investor" gate does not compute what the hypothesis describes.

This is a one-operator substitution inside the archive's already-tested best signal (Cash-Insured Innovation Value), and because cash-to-assets is highly persistent the five-year minimum will be nearly collinear with the current level, so the "funding security vs. funding level" distinction it claims to test is unlikely to be identifiable.

R&D intensity is one of the most persistent firm characteristics, so TS_MIN(xrd/at,5) is effectively a proxy for the R&D-intensity level already used in several archive signals (and mostly just separates R&D from non-R&D firms via the zero floor), making this a near-rediscovery of value × R&D intensity rather than a new economic statistic.

The one-sided worst-case revenue-growth conditioner is internally consistent with the stated sign and is a genuine diagnostic repair of the failed two-sided volatility version, though it overlaps meaningfully with fundamental-volatility/distress screens and worst-case revenue contraction may proxy for realized bad news rather than absent customer capital.

The minimum-of-ranks aggregation is a substantively different (conjunctive rather than compensatory) combination rule with a falsifiable economic claim and clear interpretation either way, and the expression's direction is consistent with the positive expected sign, despite the mild kitchen-sink risk of stacking three previously tested conditioners.

Netting cash and purchased intangibles out of assets leaves what is essentially tangible asset turnover, so this reduces to the well-known value × asset-turnover (DuPont/quality) composite rather than a new inference about off-balance-sheet capital, and the revt denominator is fragile for low-revenue firms even after winsorization.

The expression is malformed (trailing comma in `ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0), )`), and the core idea — a multi-year average earnings numerator over current price — is the long-documented cyclically-adjusted/normalized earnings-yield anomaly bolted onto the archive's existing best conditioner, so both the construction and the novelty are weak.

Economically coherent and internally consistent, but it is essentially the gen-5 Weakest-Link signal with two of three conditioner slots swapped for other already-tested archive components (cliff ratio, revenue-growth floor) while retaining the identical value leg, margin floor and MIN rule, so it will likely be highly correlated with the existing signal and tests no genuinely new mechanism.

As a "controlled experiment" it is miscalibrated — nested SUMRANK does not average the three conditioners equally (the cliff rank gets roughly double the weight of the two floors), so the comparison against the MIN version does not cleanly identify conjunctive vs compensatory reliability — and the resulting object is a generic value-plus-quality composite whose components have each already been tested additively in the archive.

A genuine reformulation rather than a cosmetic variant: it nets hidden organic knowledge capital against overstated purchased intangibles in one continuous, full-coverage measure with a well-defined zero point, and it is economically distinct from the peer-excess soft-book conditioner, though the reviewer should verify it is not simply proxying raw R&D intensity since the xrd-stock term will dominate the difference.

The residual-claim correction to the asset-backing anchor is a legitimate economic fix and the fixed margin floor keeps the comparison clean, but subtracting total debt over market cap converts much of the numerator into a negative net-leverage term, so the signal risks collapsing into a known low-leverage/distress-avoidance factor rather than an asset-cheapness anchor — diagnose the leverage loading before crediting any improvement.

This is a single-operator edit (RANK to IND_RANK on the R&D-intensity gate) of the already-tested gen-5 Refinancing Cliff signal — exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against — and the stated motivation is metric-chasing on fmb_tstat rather than a new economic mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Peer Innovator Interaction With Margin Floor
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnosis (high slope, modest alpha implies deteriorating businesses in the extreme deciles) is plausible and the hybrid of a multiplicative peer-relative interaction with an additive survival floor is structurally new, but it remains largely a mechanical blend of two already-tested archive signals, so any improvement must be shown to exceed a simple average of their standalone performance.

This is a one-leg substitution inside the already-tested "Cheapness as a Binding Constraint" structure (MIN of value, cash-vs-current-debt, and a third conditioner), with the replacement leg itself taken directly from another archive signal, so it tests no new economic claim and amounts to a cosmetic variant chasing ~1.5pp of coverage.

The state-contingent penalty is internally consistent (NEG(IND_ADJ(margin)) > 0 correctly switches the penalty on only for below-peer-margin firms) and makes a genuinely new claim — that acquired-intangible softness is informative only conditional on failed pricing power — rather than re-running the archive's linear soft-book penalty, though the ~50% mass at exactly zero in the conditioner will make its rank contribution coarse.

A defensible diagnosis-driven repair — moving the creditor claim out of the asset-backing numerator (where it destroyed the gen-6 signal's slope) into a bounded tangible-collateral screen — but it is essentially a recombination of two existing archive components (the gross liquid+knowledge anchor and the debt-to-tangible-assets conditioner) with a predictable outcome.

Scaling R&D by the gross profit pool rather than assets is a genuinely different normalization that maps directly onto the size of the reported-versus-economic earnings wedge, and the expression matches the hypothesis; the main risk is denominator instability and sign flips when gross profit is small or negative, which winsorization only partly controls, and residual correlation with plain low-margin firms.

This swaps two of three hurdles in the already-evaluated "Innovation Safety Hurdle Count" for marginal coverage gain (0.128 → 0.143) while reusing the same discrete-hurdle architecture and the same composition leg proposed elsewhere in this batch; it is an ablation of a tested signal, not a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Bounded Peer Innovator With Margin Floor
critic_notes.rationale: Product-versus-minimum on identical inputs is a legitimate structural question, but the stated motivation is internally shaky — both IND_RANK legs are already bounded in [0,1], so the product cannot be driven by "extremity" the way the reasoning claims, and the family's weak Sharpe more plausibly comes from the margin-floor leg — leaving this a functional-form tweak of an already-evaluated archive signal.

This is a direct additive splice of two already-archived gen-7 signals that share the same value construct, and the two legs are mechanically entangled — a high xrd/gross-profit ratio mechanically inflates the ib+xrd numerator of the persistence leg — so any gain is likely double-counted R&D loading rather than a new economic channel.

The `x − IND_ADJ(x)` construction correctly recovers the industry mean and the sign matches the hypothesis, but since firm-level and peer-excess soft-book conditioners are both already in the archive this is the arithmetic residual of tested pieces, and a near-constant-within-industry conditioner risks turning the spread into a sector tilt rather than a firm-level mispricing signal.

The claim that (EBITDA+R&D)/EV "has never been tested" is false — it is precisely the valuation leg inside the gen-7 "Overpriced Unproductive Soft Book" signal — and enterprise-multiple × R&D-conditioner combinations have already been run twice (gen-0 and gen-3), so the marginal information here is a denominator swap rather than a new mechanism.

The amortization adjustment is internally consistent (5-year stock, 5-year straight-line charge equals the 5-year mean outlay) and genuinely changes the ranking relative to every archive add-back, though the reviewer should note it algebraically reduces to plain E/P plus an R&D-acceleration term, so the result should be diagnosed against a raw ib/P benchmark to confirm the amortization term is doing the work.

R&D-to-market-value is a published anomaly (Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis 2001) and industry-demeaning it does not change that, while both legs share market capitalization in the denominator so the composite mostly double-loads inverse price rather than isolating a peer-relative pricing error for knowledge capital.

Applying the validated binding-constraint form to new components is a legitimate test and the MIN operator matches the stated "fail on any one" logic, but requiring a high xrd/gross-profit rank as a hard gate both narrows the long leg to heavy R&D firms and re-imports the same mechanical R&D overlap with the add-back numerator, so a coverage and composition diagnostic is mandatory.

Internally consistent and the three legs are genuinely non-overlapping in variables, but it is essentially a mechanical three-way splice of the archive's top-performing components chosen on realized metrics, so it carries obvious selection/overfitting risk and offers limited new economic content.

The conjunctive-aggregation question was already answered twice in the archive (weakest-link and binding-constraint signals), and two of the three legs here are conceptually the same as the gen-8 MIN composite (persistence, funding adequacy), so the marginal evidence is a leg substitution rather than a new test.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Discount on a Hard Balance Sheet
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archived Hard-Book Value Composite with the value leg swapped for its five-year minimum — a cosmetic variant of two already-tested signals whose likely outcome is a blend of their known metrics.

Both legs share the same market-cap denominator, so the "two independent views" framing overstates the construct — the composite is largely a double-weighted 1/P (value/size) tilt built from two already-tested anchors, i.e., a standard composite-value rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

The conditioner correctly and cleanly isolates the discrete set of firms that flip from reported loss to pre-R&D profit (it can only take values 0 or 1 given xrd ≥ 0), which is a genuinely untested classification-margin hypothesis, though the binary rank creates a large tie mass so the tilt will be modest and the group overlaps with known loss/distress effects that could push against the expected sign.

This sits directly at the intersection of two archived signals (Peer-Relative Cheap Innovator and Persistently Cheap Innovator), differing only by substituting TS_MIN for the current-year yield inside an existing IND_RANK product, which is the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against.
